references.text: The same principle applies to bearing one's guilt when a peace offering is eaten on the third day, and that it shall not be credited to the one who offered it.
Whoever eats of the flesh of the peace offering while unclean shall be cut off from their people - the same penalty as in Leviticus 19:8.
Desecration of what is holy results in being cut off from the Lord's presence.
Warns against desecrating what is holy, with death as the consequence.
Whoever sins deliberately mocks the Lord and shall be cut off from their people because they have despised the Lord's word.
Desecration of the Lord's sanctuary results in being cut off from Israel.
Desecration of the Sabbath results in being cut off from the people - the same term 'nikreta' is used.
The first occurrence of the expression 'cut off from their people' in connection with covenant breaking.
Whoever dishonors the blood of God's Son and regards the blood of the covenant as unclean deserves a far harsher punishment.
